---
title: "Week 10 Exercises - Git and GitHub"
---

Short, **ungraded** practice tasks - about 30 minutes. Companion reading: [Ch. 20](../book/chapters/20-git-github.html); reference: [App. I](../book/chapters/appendix-I-git.html). Version-controlling your term project as you finish it is the best possible practice.

1.  Check that Git is installed (`git --version`), then introduce yourself: `git config --global user.name "..."` and `git config --global user.email "..."` (use the email of your GitHub account).
2.  Turn your course folder into a repository: `cd ~/projects/comptools && git init`. Run `git status` and read what it says.
3.  Create a `.gitignore` that excludes `data/` (large files do not belong in Git) and any `.DS_Store` files.
4.  Stage and commit: `git add .` then `git commit -m "First commit: course project skeleton"`.
5.  Make an account at <https://github.com> if you do not have one, and create a new, empty repository named `comptools`.
6.  Connect and push, following GitHub's "push an existing repository" instructions (`git remote add origin ...`, `git push -u origin main`). Refresh the page - your files should appear.
7.  Edit your `README.md` locally, commit the change, and push again. Find the change in the **History** view on GitHub.
8.  Now edit the README *on GitHub* (the pencil icon), commit there, and `git pull` locally. Look at `git log --oneline` - you should see both commits.
9.  Create a branch (`git switch -c experiment`), change a file, commit, switch back to `main`, and merge it.
10. Deliberately break something: delete a tracked file with `rm`, then rescue it with `git restore <file>`. This is the safety net that makes the rest of the course's habits pay off.
